rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should explore a balanced multimodal configuration with standard encoders (scvi_n200 and resnet50) and aggregation/fusion methods (avgpool and weighted) to establish a baseline. This tests the effectiveness of combining RNA and image data with these components, clarifying if multimodal approaches outperform single-modality baselines.

The existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings and scvi_n200 RNA encoder achieve moderate accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests replacing the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l, which may capture more complex spatial patterns. It clarifies whether a larger vision transformer-based encoder improves performance, balancing exploration of critical components while staying within the multimodal, multiprofile framework.

The existing evidence shows config_009 (validation accuracy 0.706) is the current best. This experiment tests changing aggregation from avgpool to transformer while keeping RNA/image encoders and fusion method identical, which could improve modality interaction. It directly builds on config_009's successful configuration, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of aggregation methods.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l image encoder and transformer aggregation significantly improves accuracy (config_041: 0.725). This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder to pca_n2000 (vs. scvi_n200 in config_041) further improves performance while maintaining ViT and transformer settings. It clarifies if RNA encoder choices are critical beyond image encoder and aggregation, balancing exploration of RNA encoder variations with exploitation of proven effective components.

The existing evidence shows config_041 (0.725) is the top performer with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. This experiment tests whether using pca_n2000 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder (vs scvi_n200 and imagenet_vit_l in config_041) could further improve accuracy. It clarifies the impact of RNA/image encoder choices while maintaining the effective aggregation/fusion strategy. This balances exploration of key components with exploitation of the current best setup.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using 'transformer' aggregation and 'weighted' fusion (e.g., config_041) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder from 'scvi_n200' to 'scgpt' in config_041's successful setup, exploring whether the RNA encoder choice is a key factor. This balances exploitation of the transformer/weighted pattern with exploration of alternative encoders, prioritizing high-impact design choices.

The existing evidence shows config_041 (0.7249) is the best so far with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, singleprofile, and weighted fusion, exploring if changing the RNA encoder while keeping high-performing image encoder and fusion method could yield improvements. It balances exploitation of the effective image encoder and fusion while exploring RNA encoder variation.

The existing evidence shows that using transformer aggregation with imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_041) achieves the highest accuracy so far. This experiment tests whether switching to resnet50 image encoder while keeping transformer aggregation and scvi_n200 RNA encoder could yield comparable or better performance, clarifying the impact of image encoder choice on accuracy. It balances exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of a key design choice.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using 'transformer' aggregation and 'imagenet_vit_l' image encoder (e.g., config_041) achieve the highest accuracy. This experiment tests 'transformer' aggregation with 'concat' fusion using 'resnet50' image encoder, which could clarify if changing the fusion method or image encoder impacts performance. It is the best use of the remaining budget to explore critical design choices (fusion method) in a high-performing setup.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_041) achieve the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, aggregation None, and fusion concat, which could clarify if switching RNA encoders or aggregation methods impacts performance. It is the best use of the final experiment to explore critical design choices with remaining budget.
